cleanIntro: Henry's H006/H012 book. This is a centerfire tube-fed lever gun on a transfer-bar safety — there is no half-cock and no crossbolt. Note what this book does NOT contain: unlike the .22 books it publishes no receiver-cover teardown, so the Big Boy is cleaned assembled.

steps.title: Transfer bar, and what it means for carrying
steps.action: Understand the safety before you handle it. The Big Boy has a transfer-bar system: it fires only with the hammer fully cocked and the trigger pulled, so it is designed to be carried with the hammer fully down. There is no half-cock notch and no crossbolt on this rifle — if you go looking for the .22 Henry's 1/4-cock Safety position you will not find it, and resting the hammer part way is not a safety here.
steps.quote: This rifle can be safely carried fully loaded with the hammer in the fired down resting position. Please note that this rifle does not have a half cock safety position nor a crossbolt safety.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — TRANSFER BAR SAFETY, p.7

steps.title: Lever swung down and back to see what comes out
steps.action: Before anything else, point the muzzle safely, swing the lever down and pull it back. If a cartridge ejects, the rifle was loaded and you now have to empty the magazine tube as well as the chamber. Do this first every time — a tube gun gives no external sign of how many rounds it is holding.
steps.quote: Prior to loading your rifle, make certain that it is not already loaded. Point the muzzle in a safe direction, swing the lever down, and pull it back.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — PRIOR TO LOADING YOUR HENRY BIG BOY RIFLE, p.8

steps.title: Hammer fully down, inner magazine tube withdrawn
steps.action: With the hammer resting fully down, point the rifle upward and withdraw the brass inner magazine tube from the outer tube under the barrel. Rotate it to disengage before pulling. Then tip the rifle down and let the cartridges run out — .357 and .44 cases are heavy enough to come out briskly, so catch them rather than letting them hit the floor.
steps.prose: This rifle is a tubular feed design, using a brass inner magazine tube. Cartridges are loaded into the cutout in the blued outer magazine tube located underneath the barrel.
steps.quote: To unload the magazine and chamber, the hammer should be resting in the fired down position. With the rifle pointing upward, withdraw the inner magazine tube.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD THE MAGAZINE AND CHAMBER OF YOUR HENRY BIG BOY RIFLE, p.8

steps.title: Tube checked for a stuck round, then the action cycled repeatedly
steps.action: Before the inner tube goes back, look into the outer tube and make sure no cartridge is hung up inside it — a stuck round is the failure mode this check exists for, and pushing the inner tube back in on top of one is how you jam a loaded cartridge in the magazine. Then cycle the lever several times and confirm the chamber is empty.
steps.quote: Before replacing the inner magazine tube, always check it to be certain that no cartridges are stuck in the magazine tube. Open the action again, by cycling the lever, to make certain that there are no cartridges in the chamber. Cycle the action multiple times to insure that no live rounds remain in the chamber.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD THE MAGAZINE AND CHAMBER OF YOUR HENRY BIG BOY RIFLE (heading p.8), p.9

steps.title: Action open, hammer down, ammunition away
steps.action: Open the action, confirm the rifle is completely unloaded and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere safe for the rest of the job. Get the ammunition out of the cleaning area first — you are about to work the action repeatedly with solvent on your hands, and this is not the moment to have live rounds within reach.
steps.quote: OPEN THE ACTION AND MAKE CERTAIN YOUR FIREARM IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED. KEEP THE MUZZLE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CLEANING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, p.10
steps.warn: NEVER TEST THE MECHANICAL FUNCTION OF YOUR RIFLE WITH LIVE AMMUNITION.

steps.title: Lever cycled forward to open the action, bore and chamber inspected
steps.action: Swing the lever forward to hold the action open. That is the whole of the mechanical preparation this rifle gets — the Big Boy is cleaned assembled. Look into the chamber and down the bore first: centerfire pistol cartridges in a rifle barrel leave both powder fouling and, with jacketed bullets, copper.
steps.aside: NOTICE! It is very important that the bore of your rifle be cleaned thoroughly and promptly after shooting.
steps.quote: For cleaning, we suggest that you first open the action by cycling the lever forward. Inspect the chamber and bore for brass, copper and powder fouling.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY, p.11

steps.title: Bore cleaned breech to muzzle, the way the bullet went
steps.action: Pull the patch through from the breech toward the muzzle. Henry states the rule and the reason: cleaning muzzle-to-breech drags the fouling back out of the barrel into the chamber and the action, where it works into the carrier and the lockwork. A pull-through kit handles the side-ejecting action better than a rod does.
steps.prose: To properly clean from breech to muzzle, use a pull-though cleaning kit, such as those available on www.henrypride.com.
steps.quote: WHENEVER POSSIBLE, CLEAN THE BORE IN THE DIRECTION OF BULLET TRAVEL.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY, p.11

steps.title: Bolt wiped and lightly oiled
steps.action: Wipe the bolt clean with solvent on a patch or rag, paying attention to the recess around the firing pin where carbon collects, then oil it lightly. Do not flood it — excess oil here drains into the trigger mechanism and towards the wood, and the manual warns about both on the same page.
steps.quote: Wipe the bolt clean of any debris with solvent and a patch or small rag. Lightly oil bolt.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY, p.11

steps.title: Do not use aggressive solvents
steps.action: Stick to a mild, well-known bore solvent. Aggressive cleaners will attack the finishes on this rifle — the Big Boy carries a brass or hardened-brass receiver depending on variant, alongside blued steel, and a solvent chosen for stripping heavy carbon does not distinguish between fouling and a decorative finish.
steps.quote: IMPORTANT - PLEASE NOTE THAT IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO TAKE YOUR HENRY LEVER ACTION APART TO KEEP IT CLEAN. IMPORTANT - DO NOT USE AGGRESSIVE SOLVENTS.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY, p.10

steps.title: Locking bolt: if it ever comes out, it goes back in
steps.action: If any work on this rifle involves the locking bolt, it must be reinstalled before the rifle is fired again. Henry prints this as a standalone warning in capitals, which is the measure of it: the locking bolt is what holds the breech shut against a centerfire cartridge, and firing without it is not a malfunction, it is an open breech.
steps.quote: WARNING: REMOVAL AND FAILURE TO RE-INSTALL THE LOCKING BOLT (PART 35) IS EXTREMELY DANGEROUS.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — SIGHTS AND SIGHT ADJUSTMENTS, p.9

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is everything Henry publishes for cleaning the Big Boy, and it is all done with the rifle assembled. Unlike the .22 Henry books, this manual gives no receiver-cover removal and no takedown of any kind — it says the rifle need not come apart, then goes straight to solvent choice. There is no deeper owner procedure to follow, so there is no Deep Clean branch here.
steps.quote: NOTICE! DO NOT ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: Henry H006 & Legacy H012 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY, p.10

deepAbsentReason: Henry's H006/H012 book publishes NO disassembly procedure at all. On printed p.10 the sentence 'IMPORTANT - PLEASE NOTE THAT IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO TAKE YOUR HENRY LEVER ACTION APART TO KEEP IT CLEAN.' is followed immediately by 'IMPORTANT - DO NOT USE AGGRESSIVE SOLVENTS.' In the H001 and H004 manuals the identical opening sentence continues into a receiver-cover teardown ('SHOULD YOU WISH TO TAKE IT APART, UNSCREW THE RECEIVER COVER TANG SCREW...'); this book stops. That teardown was NOT carried across: it is a sibling model's procedure sitting inside near-identical boilerplate, which is exactly the substitution shape the rules forbid, and the Big Boy is a centerfire rifle with a different safety system and different receiver material from the .22s. The book's only other disassembly-adjacent text is the p.9 warning that failing to re-install the locking bolt is extremely dangerous, and the p.10 instruction to take the rifle to a gunsmith if further disassembly is required. No deep procedure exists to author.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Pull a solvent-damp patch breech to muzzle, following bullet travel
Work at copper fouling with a fresh patch face each pass — jacketed pistol bullets leave it
Dry the bore, then leave a light film of oil

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Wipe carbon from the bolt face and the firing pin recess, then oil lightly
Wipe the carrier and reachable receiver interior with the lever open
Use a mild solvent only — no aggressive cleaners near the receiver finish

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBES & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the brass inner magazine tube dry and check it is not bent
Check the outer tube and loading port are clear of a stuck cartridge
Leave a film of oil on exposed steel; wipe the wood dry

reassembly: Push the inner magazine tube back down into position and lock it into place.
Close the action and confirm the lever seats fully home against the receiver.
Lower the hammer fully down — this rifle has no half-cock, so fully down is the carry position.
Wipe off handling marks and leave the exposed steel under a light film of oil.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty, cycle the lever through full travel several times and confirm it closes fully home, check the inner magazine tube is seated and locked, and confirm the hammer falls only when it is fully cocked and the trigger is pulled.
